title: An Incremental Multi-Level, Multi-Scale Approach to Assessment of Multifidelity HPC Systems
problem: Analyzing terabyte-scale monitoring data collected at multiple fidelity levels and temporal resolutions from large-scale HPC systems to identify meaningful spatial-temporal patterns is computationally expensive and produces high-dimensional outputs that are difficult to interpret.
motivation: Understanding system behavior in increasingly complex large-scale HPC systems is critical for performance optimization, diagnostics, and effective system management.
method: The paper develops I-mrDMD (incremental multiresolution dynamic mode decomposition), which incrementally processes high-dimensional monitoring data to extract spatial-temporal patterns across different frequency ranges. Algorithm outputs are integrated with D3-based visualization in Jupyter Notebooks to align and visually display processed hardware, job, and environment logs through a generalizable rack visualization approach.
key_novelty: Incremental implementation of multiresolution dynamic mode decomposition (I-mrDMD) for prompt analysis of terabyte-scale HPC system monitoring data.
contributions: Incremental mrDMD algorithm that processes massive monitoring datasets incrementally without storing full data history
Integration of multiresolution decomposition with multi-modal log visualization for HPC systems
Generalized rack-level visualization framework combining hardware, job, and environment logs
Validation and demonstration on real Cray XC40 (Theta) supercomputer with practical use scenarios

metrics.other: efficacy demonstrated through real-world use scenarios on Theta supercomputer

primary_theme: Incremental temporal-spatial pattern extraction for HPC monitoring
